diagnoses: COVID-19 with acute respiratory distress syndrome
brief: A 45-year-old patient with COVID-19 needs airway management and ventilator care. Learners practice protective equipment use, intubation, managing low blood pressure after induction, ARDS treatment, and team communication.
A reproductive-age woman presents with abnormal uterine bleeding. Students take a history, build a differential diagnosis, write a postencounter note, and get feedback from the SP.

diagnoses: Abdominal pain without a confirmed diagnosis
brief: A patient with abdominal pain is being discharged from the emergency department without a diagnosis. Students practice explaining diagnostic uncertainty using a checklist in peer role-play.

exclude_reason: Inpatient coding curriculum, no patient case

brief: An older adult with dementia has dysphagia and is on modified diets. Residents work through evaluation and treatment choices and discuss the limited evidence for thickened liquids.

diagnoses: Toxic stress from adverse childhood experiences
brief: A patient with a history of childhood adversity is discussed in a facilitated virtual small group. Students practice screening for toxic stress and buffering factors and use brief resilience tools.

diagnoses: Endocrine conditions including diabetes and thyroid disease
brief: Spanish-speaking patients with endocrine problems are portrayed in role-play interviews. Students practice taking histories, explaining diagnoses, and giving discharge instructions in Spanish.
Patients with social needs such as housing or food problems are presented as cases. Students practice assessing these needs and linking patients to community resources.

diagnoses: Opioid use disorder, pain with early refill request
brief: A patient with pain asks for an early refill of an opioid medication. Students explore their own biases in a progressive case presentation, and third-year students run the same vignettes as OSCEs.
Video cases show patients with alcohol use disorder in clinic. Residents discuss medication options and treatment decisions.

diagnoses: Firearm injury risk, safe storage counseling
brief: A trauma patient is counseled on safe firearm storage. Providers practice the counseling conversation with standardized patients after a short lecture.
Three online modules end in patient case applications on safe opioid prescribing, opioid use disorder, and pain management. Learners apply CDC guideline advice to patient decisions.

exclude_reason: Peer suicide prevention role-play, no patient

brief: A patient has shingles and asks about treatment. Students recommend an antiviral and answer the patient questions about how it works and its side effects.

diagnoses: Low-acuity conditions in virtual urgent care
presentations: minor acute illness by video visit
brief: Standardized patients present low-acuity problems to physicians in a virtual urgent care clinic. Physicians practice telemedicine visits and get feedback on communication and disease-specific skills.

A standardized patient with opioid use disorder is seen in a medicine clerkship OSCE. Students practice motivational interviewing, harm reduction talk, and nonstigmatizing language, then document the visit.

diagnoses: Gender-affirming primary care for transgender and genderqueer patients
brief: Several patient versions share one health history but differ in gender identity and sex assigned at birth. Students practice inclusive communication, discuss hormone therapy, and give preventive care advice.
Two case modules present a patient with a disability and a provider with a disability. Learners discuss ableism, accommodations, and barriers to care.
A patient with opioid use disorder is discussed in a large-group case session. Students apply physiology and pharmacology to diagnosis and treatment with medications for OUD.
A transgender patient seeks gender-affirming care in primary care. Residents practice history taking, affirming communication, and hormone prescribing with a standardized patient.
Interactive virtual patients present women with urogynecologic problems. Students work through diagnosis and nonsurgical and surgical management options.
A parent is asked for informed consent before a pediatric procedure such as lumbar puncture or laceration repair. Residents practice the consent conversation in a recorded OSCE.

diagnoses: Cardiac emergencies in the postanesthesia unit
brief: Three ACLS scenarios involve adult patients in a postanesthesia care unit. Learners use rapid cycle practice to improve teamwork, leadership, defibrillator use, and treatment.

A 28-year-old woman on infertility treatment arrives in the emergency department with shortness of breath and near fainting. Residents use bedside ultrasound to reach the diagnosis and start treatment.

exclude_reason: Ventilator equipment troubleshooting, no patient case

presentations: reproductive autonomy and access to care
brief: Four cases explore reproductive justice issues such as sterilization, maternal health, and access to family planning. Students discuss the key points of each case in small groups.
Junior residents lead the resuscitation of a critically ill patient across four simulations. They practice crisis resource management, leadership, and team communication.
A patient has critical hypoglycemia and needs urgent care. First-year students work as an interprofessional team using an ISBARR huddle to communicate and act.

diagnoses: Chlamydia and other sexually transmitted infections
brief: Cases involve sexually active patients at risk for STIs. Residents practice advanced sexual history taking, site-specific testing, and counseling including partner therapy.
A parent is hesitant about childhood vaccines. Pediatric residents practice vaccine communication in role-play and are assessed with a standardized patient.

presentations: altered mental status from lithium poisoning
brief: A patient on chronic lithium therapy has acute-on-chronic lithium poisoning. Residents recognize the toxicity and manage it in the emergency department.

diagnoses: Patient microaggressions toward a health care team member
presentations: patient expressing bias during a visit
brief: Standardized patients express microaggressions toward a member of the care team. Residents practice bystander responses using the WAKE framework and debrief each scenario.
A hypothetical primary care patient faces a medical stressor. Small groups role-play the encounter to build a coping plan using the stress and coping model.
Video-recorded anesthesia simulation scenarios drive faculty-led case discussions. Students in a virtual clerkship review the patient cases and discuss management.

diagnoses: Over-the-counter product use in young children
brief: A parent calls about over-the-counter products for a young child. Students practice counseling in a simulated parent call OSCE after a video curriculum.
An infant has bronchiolitis with worsening respiratory distress, shown on a high-fidelity simulator. Students assess the child and decide when to escalate respiratory support.

diagnoses: Cardiac, respiratory, gastrointestinal, and genitourinary presentations
brief: Four modules with four standardized patient cases each cover common presenting symptoms. Student pairs take a focused history, ask for exam findings, and build a differential diagnosis.

presentations: asthma symptoms needing medication step up
brief: Cases involve children with asthma who need symptom-based treatment changes. Residents discuss the 2020 guideline updates on intermittent steroids and single maintenance and reliever therapy.
A standardized patient learns of a miscarriage diagnosis, in person or by video. Students break the bad news using the SPIKES protocol and discuss treatment options.
Children and teens present with common behavioral and mental health problems. Residents work through cases and role-play in a seminar followed by monthly case discussions.
Three patients with urgent needs also carry trauma related to abuse, transgender status, or discrimination. Students take histories, examine patients, and apply trauma-informed care.

diagnoses: Chronic low back pain with possible opioid misuse
brief: A patient with chronic low back pain after a car accident keeps taking opioids without benefit and shows possible misuse behaviors. Interprofessional student teams interview the SP online and build a shared plan.
A 15-year-old girl arrives in the emergency department with agitation and hallucinations. The team performs a primary survey, recognizes the anticholinergic toxidrome, and treats complications.
Case-based sessions cover emergency OB/GYN problems seen in the emergency department. Residents work through cases with review questions in a game format.

presentations: hand pain with erythema and edema
brief: A 47-year-old man has hand pain and skin changes from unrecognized radiation exposure. Residents diagnose and manage the hematopoietic and cutaneous forms of acute radiation syndrome.
An unfolding patient case presents several points of clinical uncertainty. Students classify the type of uncertainty and discuss how they would problem-solve each one.

diagnoses: Osteomyelitis in pediatric sickle cell disease
presentations: bone pain in a child with sickle cell disease
brief: A child with sickle cell disease has osteomyelitis and is at risk of biased care. Learners diagnose and treat the complication while practicing bias-aware communication.

diagnoses: Second-trimester fetal demise needing dilation and evacuation
brief: A 29-year-old woman at 18 weeks has fetal demise and needs a dilation and evacuation. Residents perform the procedure with a team and manage an unexpected hemorrhage.

diagnoses: Acute pain in the emergency department
brief: A patient with acute pain is followed from arrival to discharge. Students build an analgesic plan using a structured acute pain approach.
Pediatric neurology cases are discussed with video demonstrations of telehealth exams. Residents practice remote neurologic assessment and decisions.

diagnoses: Hypovolemic shock in a malnourished child
Child death in a resource-limited setting
brief: A malnourished 5-year-old is in hypovolemic shock, deteriorates, and dies. Residents practice care in a low-resource setting and communication with the family, then debrief.

diagnoses: Toddler fracture with biased concern for abuse
brief: A toddler in an African American family has a classic toddler fracture, and a consultant pushes for a child welfare report. Learners identify that it is not abuse and address the implicit bias.

diagnoses: Geriatric multimorbidity in a telemedicine visit
brief: An older adult with multiple conditions is seen by video. Students practice a telemedicine encounter, adapting to technology and sensory or cognitive barriers and involving caregivers.
A trained simulated patient and a lay caregiver take part in a discharge encounter. First-year residents practice discharge planning and communication.

presentations: fever and altered mental status after respiratory infection
brief: A 28-year-old man develops bacterial meningitis after an upper respiratory infection. Students recognize and manage it using a high-fidelity simulator and a standardized participant for the patient voice.
Patients need involuntary psychiatric admission and are portrayed by standardized patients. Residents practice explaining the plan using a structured protocol across three scenarios.
A transgender or gender-diverse patient wants to discuss hormone therapy. Students assess the patient goals and practice inclusive communication with a standardized patient.

exclude_reason: Moral injury workshop, no patient case

presentations: death or serious injury news after a bicycle collision
brief: A patient injured in a bicycle collision receives bad news from the student in a standardized patient encounter. Students also learn how to counsel victims of intimate partner violence.
Three scenarios run in sequence: a resuscitation, two trauma patients, and a bad news conversation. Senior residents practice task switching and are assessed with checklists.

exclude_reason: Cardiac exam curriculum, no defined case

diagnoses: Social determinants of health needs in a non-English speaking patient
brief: Patients who prefer Spanish, Tagalog, French, or Igbo are seen by video with an interpreter. Students practice interpreter use and address social needs.
A patient seeks contraceptive counseling. Clerkship students practice person-centered counseling with a standardized patient after an online module.
Three interactive cases cover reproductive endocrinology and infertility. Facilitators lead learners through diagnosis and management, in person or virtually.

diagnoses: Upper gastrointestinal bleed with airway blood
brief: A 55-year-old man with alcohol use has hematemesis and sudden blood in the airway during endoscopy. Residents manage the difficult airway and perform a cricothyrotomy as a last resort.
A patient must be told about a medical error. Fourth-year students practice disclosure in an OSCE and then join a case-based debrief with role-play.

diagnoses: Pediatric polytrauma with burns, carbon monoxide and cyanide toxicity
presentations: child extracted from a van fire
brief: A child is pulled from a burning van after a crash. Learners manage the airway, burns, abdominal bleeding, and carbon monoxide and cyanide poisoning.
Two children need sedation for a shoulder dislocation and a forearm fracture. Fellows set up, dose propofol or ketamine, and manage sedation complications.

diagnoses: Acute agitation in an adolescent awaiting psychiatric placement
brief: A teenager admitted for suicidal thoughts becomes acutely agitated. Residents try verbal de-escalation and choose a medication to reduce agitation.
A 27-year-old man bitten by a dog develops muscle rigidity from tetanus. Students consider tetanus in the differential and manage its complications.
Virtual patients present deficits in each of the 12 cranial nerves. Students test nerve function and diagnose the deficit with immediate feedback.

diagnoses: Inflicted head and abdominal trauma in an infant
brief: Two pediatric trauma resuscitations feature a 12-month-old with inflicted injuries and an 18-month-old with gunshot wounds. Teams practice communication and timely care, one case in traditional format and one with rapid cycle practice.
Standardized patients receive disclosure of a medical error, and a peer version covers disclosure to colleagues. Learners practice honesty, empathy, and apology using rapid cycle practice.
A patient with dyslipidemia is managed through a team-based learning encounter. Students review labs and risk factors, plan a diet, and assess inheritance patterns.

exclude_reason: Anatomy case session, no patient encounter

diagnoses: Somatoform disorder with body image concerns
brief: An outpatient presents with body image concerns. Students step through the history, mental status exam, and differential diagnosis with feedback questions.
Five simulated cases follow children through an initial visit and several follow-ups. Residents practice diagnosing and managing common pediatric behavioral and mental health problems.
Cases in vascular tumors and malformations are discussed by pediatric trainees. Residents work through diagnosis and referral in small and large groups.

diagnoses: Social determinants of health in specialty clerkships
presentations: social needs during a clinical visit
brief: Role-play vignettes for each clerkship include a history and exam. Students practice eliciting social determinants of health from patients.
Students from six professions each interview a simulated patient while others observe. They compare what each profession notices and asks.
A pregnancy case covers normal care, labor, and select complications. Clerkship students work through it in a flipped classroom small group.
An agitated patient is portrayed by a standardized patient in a psychiatry clerkship. Students practice verbal de-escalation and get peer and SP feedback.

exclude_reason: Bias response workshop, no clinical case

diagnoses: Health care needs of LGBTQ+ youth
brief: LGBTQ+ youth cases are discussed in small groups and with a patient and caregiver panel. Learners practice patient-centered care for these young people.
A child has a burn injury that may be from abuse. Physicians learn to tell abusive burns from accidental ones through an interactive case.

presentations: hypotension on a rapid response call
brief: Two simulations feature an adult patient with hypotension, one with septic shock and one with cardiogenic shock. Interns use a decision framework and communication skills during a rapid response.

diagnoses: Stunned myocardium from acute severe anemia
presentations: low blood pressure during hip replacement
brief: A 73-year-old man having elective hip replacement loses blood and develops acute heart injury. Residents adjust the anesthetic plan and manage the cardiac complication.

diagnoses: Chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear exposure
brief: A small-group case study follows patients exposed to CBRN agents. Students evaluate and treat using a worksheet and clinical guidelines.
A case unfolds in two parts, with medical and pharmacy students holding different information. Students communicate to build a differential diagnosis together.
A patient holds misinformation about vaccines. Students role-play conversations using ask-respond-tell-seek and motivational interviewing.
Four case scenarios show how physicians shape patient experience. Residents discuss strategies to meet patients holistic needs.

presentations: brain death assessment and family communication
brief: A brain-dead patient on a mannequin and a spouse played by a confederate. The trainee explains the exam to the spouse, performs brain death testing, and communicates the findings.

presentations: child in resuscitation with family at bedside
brief: Family members are present during a pediatric resuscitation, played by simulated participants. Team members practice the family presence facilitator role in in situ simulations.

diagnoses: Pregnant trauma with tension pneumothorax and uterine rupture
brief: A pregnant trauma patient has tension pneumothorax and uterine rupture and arrests. Residents resuscitate her and perform resuscitative hysterotomy on a task trainer.

exclude_reason: Faculty workshop on responding to racism

brief: Spanish-speaking patients are seen in standardized patient practice, including a diabetic consultation OSCE station. Students communicate in Spanish and integrate gender-affirming care.
Short online clinical cases cover common musculoskeletal presentations. Students answer questions on diagnosis and anatomy after each case.
A pediatric case shows how housing, food, and other social needs affect a child. Students identify these factors and choose questions to ask the family.

learners: medicine, nursing, pharmacy, and public health students
brief: A patient is hesitant about vaccines because of misinformation. Interprofessional students practice a response with standardized patients in person and online.
A standardized patient holds misinformation about COVID-19. Interprofessional students use advanced communication techniques and work together on a response.
A patient case guides students through sedating and anesthetic drug choices. Students integrate pharmacology with clinical reasoning.
Digital simulation scenarios feature patients with temporomandibular disorders. Learners practice assessment, diagnosis, and management.
Four case-based online modules cover asthma, chronic cough, tracheostomy, and obstructive sleep apnea. Learners work through the cases with expert videos and questions.

diagnoses: Trauma-informed prenatal care after prior child welfare involvement
brief: A multiparous woman with past substance use starts prenatal care late because she lost custody of a newborn earlier. Learners practice trauma-informed care with a standardized patient.

diagnoses: Care of refugee and migrant patients with trauma histories
presentations: patient with trauma history and mistrust
brief: Refugee and migrant patients with histories of trauma are portrayed in simulation. Residents practice trauma-informed care and uncover underlying causes of distress.
Case scenarios and role-plays present patients who need lifestyle changes. Students practice counseling for health behavior change.
Students care for a laboring woman with limited English proficiency using a medical interpreter. An OSCE with standardized patients who speak other languages assesses interpretation skills.

presentations: pediatric acute illness by video visit
brief: A simulated parent and child are seen by video. Preclinical students practice telemedicine visits and get feedback from the SP and faculty.
Two standardized patient encounters involve patients with suicidal thoughts. Third-year students practice suicide assessment and management.

exclude_reason: Dilation and evacuation model, procedural only

diagnoses: Acute mental status change in an older adult
brief: An older adult presents with a change in mental status in a clinical reasoning session. Students apply the 4Ms of mentation, medications, mobility, and what matters most.
